title: Plain language - The AI Operations Manager
summary:
Second-worst page: 8 findings shown, 3 more in the file. "Agent" carries most of it.

1. "This pattern is the entry point for most agentic AI deployments in professional services."
-> "For most firms, this is the first job they hand to an AI that works on its own."

2. "The pattern extends naturally into tool-connected agents (calendar, email, project management) when those integrations are available."
-> "If your AI can connect to your calendar, email or project tools, it can do even more of this for you."

3. "...one dashboard where every agent reports its results, a simple way to add new agents, and the jobs it runs for you."
-> "...one page where every recurring AI job reports what it did, an easy way to add new jobs..."

4. "Define a recurring coordination role and assign it to AI as a persistent function - not a one-time task."
-> "Give AI a standing job - the weekly status, the meeting prep, the follow-ups - not a one-off favor."

5. "Inside Anthropic, the share of employees' AI sessions spent managing agents - writing instructions, building dashboards, monitoring pipelines - rose from 10% to 22%..."
-> "At Anthropic, the company that makes Claude, the time staff spent managing their AI helpers more than doubled in six months."

6. "Multi-step workflows, project coordination, or any recurring process that involves... routing tasks, or synthesizing inputs from multiple sources."
-> "Any work that repeats: tracking status, getting the right task to the right person, pulling notes into one summary."

7. "Async Updates" / "Route information to the right summary document or channel"
-> "Updates between meetings" / "Send each piece of news to the right summary or team chat."

8. "Explain how to add a new agent: write its one-line registration, add it to the list, and it reports to the dashboard with the same fields as every other agent."
-> "Explain how to add a new AI job: one line on what it does, when it runs and who owns it; it reports on the same page as the others."
